cards.explanation: The answer is that not one stone will be left on another. Jesus asks, “Do you see all these things?” and then says, “…not one stone here will be left on another; every one will be thrown down.” His disciples, the men following Him, had come up to point out the buildings. I think that was not what they were expecting to hear, friends.

The answer is that they ask when it will happen and what the sign will be. The disciples say, “when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of Your coming and of the end of the age?” They come to Him privately to ask. Two questions in one breath, friends, and I respect a person who stacks them up like that.

The first warning is not to let anyone deceive them. Jesus answers, “See to it that no one deceives you.” They asked about timing, and the very first thing out of His mouth is a warning. When an answer starts somewhere you didn't expect, friends, pay attention.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “For many will come in My name, claiming, ‘I am the Christ,’ and will deceive many.” Many come and many get deceived, not only a few. That's why His opening warning matters so much, friends.

The answer is don't be alarmed by it. Jesus says, “You will hear of wars and rumors of wars, but see to it that you are not alarmed.” He doesn't say the news will be light. He says not to be alarmed. You know when you refresh the news every ten seconds? That's a tall order for a lot of us, friends.
The word is end. Jesus says, “These things must happen, but the end is still to come.” So the wars aren't the end. Hearing that, friends, I'd say my shoulders just dropped an inch.

The answer is birth pains. Jesus says, “All these are the beginning of birth pains.” After wars, famines and earthquakes, He calls them the beginning of something. One word in that verse matters a lot, friends, and it's beginning.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Then they will deliver you over to be persecuted and killed, and you will be hated by all nations because of My name.” I think this one is heavy, friends, and it's okay to say so. It's also exactly what He tells them.

The word is cold. Jesus says, “Because of the multiplication of wickedness, the love of most will grow cold.” Notice He says most. I'd rather my cookies cool than my love, friends, so that's a sobering one.

The word is saved. Jesus says, “But the one who perseveres to the end will be saved.” After a verse about love growing cold, friends, that line lands like the oven door opening in winter. Warm, and just in time.

The answer is False. Jesus says, “And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a testimony to all nations, and then the end will come.” All the world and all nations is far bigger than Israel alone. The good news goes out wide, friends, and that's exactly what He says.
